summary: Wallowa County, OR tower: ODF 30-ft steel tower set up 1973, blown over that October, rebuilt 1974; later moved to Wallowa Fire Dept as a hose tower; gone by 1990.

facts.status_note: Gone by 1990. Tower moved to the Wallowa Fire Department for use as a hose tower; no source describes the original site today.
facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry (the 1973 Wallowa County Chieftain calls it a cooperative state and federal Forest Service tower)

events.note: 30-foot steel tower and trailer set up to replace the Tope Creek lookout
Tower blew over on the night of October 6, 1973, before its guy wires were tied and before it had fire-fighting equipment or windows
Tower rebuilt and back in use for the 1974 fire season
Lookout gone in 1990; the tower had by then been moved to the Wallowa Fire Department as a hose tower (move undated in the sources)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1973 ODF annual report says the tower was reconstructed at the Wallowa headquarters and would be hauled to the site. A Chieftain item quotes a state forestry spokesman saying no decision had been reached on rebuilding at the same site. The story gives both and does not pick one.

The Forest Lookouts page quotes a Wallowa County Chieftain report calling it a cooperative state and federal Forest Service tower, while the state's 1973 annual report calls it the Department's new tower. The story reports both; the record keeps Oregon Department of Forestry, which the register and Fire Lookout both give.

The register, Fire Lookout and Forest Lookouts all agree the lookout was gone by 1990 and that the tower went to the Wallowa Fire Department. No source gives a date for the move, so the story gives 1990 only as the date the lookout was gone.

notes_for_editor: The three sources agree on the 1973 build, the October 1973 blowdown, the 1974 rebuild and the 1990 removal. The only real disagreement is which agency ran the tower, and the story says so. Nothing in our sources describes the original site or the Wallowa tower today, so the 'today' paragraph says that plainly. A quick check with the Wallowa Fire Department or the Wallowa History Center would settle whether the hose tower still stands, but I did not chase that.
